Quarterly Business Performance Report
Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 2024
Prepared by the Office of Corporate Planning, Meridian Fastener Group

This report summarizes the operational and financial performance of Meridian Fastener Group for the third quarter of fiscal year 2024, covering the period from July 1 through September 30. The report has been compiled by the Office of Corporate Planning in coordination with the Finance, Operations, and Sales divisions, and is intended for internal distribution to department heads, regional managers, and members of the executive committee. The findings presented herein are based on preliminary figures and are subject to minor revision pending the final close of the fiscal quarter by the Accounting Department.

Overall, the quarter reflected a period of moderate and stable growth across most business lines, consistent with the trends observed in the preceding two quarters. Total consolidated revenue for the quarter reached $48.6 million, representing an increase of 3.1 percent over the second quarter and a 5.4 percent increase over the same period last year. This growth was driven primarily by continued demand in the Industrial Fasteners division, which contributed $27.9 million in revenue, up from $26.3 million in the prior quarter. The Specialty Hardware division posted revenue of $14.2 million, a modest increase of 1.8 percent quarter-over-quarter, while the Consumer Products division recorded revenue of $6.5 million, roughly flat relative to the second quarter.

Gross margin across the company held steady at 34.2 percent, a slight improvement from 33.7 percent in the previous quarter. This improvement is attributable in part to the renegotiated supply agreement with Halbrook Steel Supply, which took effect at the start of the quarter and resulted in a reduction of approximately 2 percent in raw material costs for high-tensile steel components. The Operations team, under the direction of Vice President of Manufacturing Renata Ostrowski, reported that the two primary production facilities in Danville and Marsh Creek operated at an average capacity utilization of 87 percent, up from 84 percent in the second quarter. This increase in utilization was supported by the completion of scheduled maintenance at the Marsh Creek facility in early August, which had been anticipated in the annual capital expenditure plan and did not result in any unplanned downtime.

On the sales and marketing front, the Regional Sales team led by Director Colin Ashworth reported continued expansion in the Midwest and Southeast territories, with new account acquisition in those regions accounting for approximately 62 percent of net new revenue generated during the quarter. The Northeast territory, by contrast, showed only marginal growth, which management attributes to softer demand in the construction sector following a period of elevated interest rates. The Sales division also noted the successful renewal of the multi-year supply contract with Corrigan Builders Alliance, one of the company's longstanding key accounts, which was finalized in late September and is expected to contribute an estimated $3.2 million in annual revenue beginning in the fourth quarter.

From a cost management perspective, selling, general, and administrative expenses totaled $9.1 million for the quarter, representing 18.7 percent of revenue, consistent with historical averages for the company. The Finance Department, led by Chief Financial Officer Priya Nandakumar, noted that the increase in administrative expenses relative to the prior quarter, which totaled $8.7 million, was primarily attributable to one-time costs associated with the implementation of the new enterprise resource planning system, a project that is expected to be substantially complete by the end of the fourth quarter. Once fully deployed, the new system is projected to reduce administrative overhead in subsequent quarters through improved inventory tracking and streamlined procurement workflows.

Operating income for the quarter was $7.4 million, yielding an operating margin of 15.2 percent, a slight improvement over the 14.6 percent margin recorded in the second quarter. Net income attributable to the parent company was $5.1 million, compared to $4.7 million in the prior quarter. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization stood at $9.8 million, representing an EBITDA margin of 20.1 percent. The Board of Directors has reviewed these figures during its quarterly meeting held on October 12 and has expressed general satisfaction with the trajectory of the company's core operating metrics, while also directing management to continue monitoring input cost volatility in the fourth quarter given ongoing fluctuations in global steel pricing.

Human resources data for the quarter indicate that total headcount across the organization stood at 1,142 employees as of September 30, a net increase of 18 positions from the prior quarter, primarily reflecting hiring within the Danville facility to support increased production volume. Employee turnover for the quarter remained within the company's historical range at 4.3 percent, and the Human Resources Department, under Director Marcus Feldt, reported no significant disruptions to staffing levels in any department.

Ticket ID: HD-88213

Initial Contact — March 4, 10:12 AM
Customer contact Diane Ostrowski of Meridian Office Supply Co. submitted a ticket via the online support portal regarding recurring discrepancies in monthly invoice totals generated by the InvoiceTrack Pro software, version 6.3.1. Ms. Ostrowski indicated that for the past three billing cycles, the automatically generated subtotal on invoices exceeding fifty line items did not match the sum of the individual line items when recalculated manually in a spreadsheet. She noted the discrepancy was small, typically between $0.01 and $0.14, but that her accounting department flagged it during month-end reconciliation and requested clarification before closing the books. Ms. Ostrowski attached three sample invoices (Invoice #10432, #10458, #10471) demonstrating the issue and requested a callback or email response within two business days per the terms of her support contract tier.

First Response — March 4, 2:47 PM
Representative Colin Vasquez reviewed the submitted invoices and confirmed the discrepancies as described. Mr. Vasquez noted that the pattern appeared consistent with a known rounding behavior in the tax calculation module when line items are grouped across multiple tax jurisdictions within a single invoice. He requested additional information from Ms. Ostrowski, specifically whether the affected invoices involved customers located in more than one state, as this would help confirm the hypothesis. He also asked whether the discrepancy occurred only on invoices generated after the January 15 software update or if it predated that release.

Customer Follow-Up — March 5, 9:03 AM
Ms. Ostrowski replied confirming that all three sample invoices involved shipments to customers in both Ohio and Pennsylvania, and that the discrepancy did not appear in any invoices prior to the January update. She stated that her department had not changed any internal settings around that time and asked whether a rollback of the update was feasible while a permanent fix was developed. She also asked whether other customers had reported the same issue, as she wanted to understand whether this was isolated to her account configuration.

Internal Escalation Note — March 5, 11:20 AM
Mr. Vasquez escalated the ticket internally to the Billing Systems Engineering team (assigned to engineer Priya Ramanathan) with a summary of the reported behavior, the version number, and the two sample invoices most clearly demonstrating the rounding inconsistency. He flagged the ticket as related to a broader pattern observed in four other accounts since the January 15 release, referencing internal tracking ticket ENG-5502 for cross-reference. He recommended against a full rollback given that the update also contained a security patch for the login authentication module, and instead requested an expedited patch timeline.

Engineering Response — March 6, 4:15 PM
Ms. Ramanathan confirmed that the rounding issue stemmed from a change in how the tax engine aggregates line-item tax before rounding, rather than rounding each line item individually before summing. She indicated that a corrective patch, version 6.3.2, was already in testing and expected to be released within five business days. In the interim, she suggested a manual workaround: generating a supplementary reconciliation report through the "Export Detailed Tax Breakdown" feature under Reports > Tax Summary, which calculates totals using the pre-aggregation method and would match manual spreadsheet totals. Mr. Vasquez was asked to relay this workaround to the customer along with an estimated timeline for the permanent fix.

Customer Communication — March 6, 5:32 PM
Mr. Vasquez emailed Ms. Ostrowski with the explanation of the rounding behavior, instructions for generating the supplementary tax breakdown report as a temporary workaround, and confirmation that a patch was expected the following week. He also clarified that the discrepancy did not affect the actual amounts charged to end customers, only the internal reconciliation totals, since the invoice PDFs themselves reflected correct final amounts. He offered to schedule a brief phone call to walk through the workaround if needed.

Customer Follow-Up — March 7, 8:41 AM
Ms. Ostrowski responded that she had tested the workaround on Invoice #10471 and confirmed the totals now matched her manual spreadsheet calculations. She thanked Mr. Vasquez for the clear explanation and stated a phone call was not necessary. She asked to be notified once version 6.3.2 was released so her team could resume using the standard report format without the extra export step.

Patch Release Notification — March 12, 9:00 AM
Mr. Vasquez sent a follow-up email confirming that version 6.3.2 had been released overnight and included the corrected tax aggregation logic. He provided a brief summary of the update changelog and noted that the update would apply automatically for accounts on the standard maintenance plan, which included Meridian Office Supply Co. He asked Ms. Ostrowski to run one test invoice after the update applied and confirm the totals matched expected values, purely as a precaution before closing the ticket.

Final Customer Confirmation — March 13, 10:55 AM
Ms. Ostrowski confirmed that Invoice #10502, generated after the update, matched manual calculations without requiring the supplementary export. She stated the issue appeared fully resolved and thanked the support team for the timely response and clear communication throughout the process. She noted no further action was needed on her end.

This memorandum summarizes the renewal terms and internal review process associated with the annual service agreement between Colworth Analytics Group and its long-standing facilities and logistics vendor, Marrow & Doyle Supply Partners. The current agreement, originally executed on March 4, 2021, and renewed twice since without material amendment, is set to expire on September 30 of this year. Following a scheduled review conducted by the Procurement and Vendor Relations team, the recommendation is to proceed with a two-year renewal under revised pricing terms, subject to final sign-off from the Finance Committee and the Director of Operations, Marguerite Okafor.

The scope of services under this agreement covers janitorial contracting, waste disposal coordination, and general facilities maintenance support for the Colworth campus located at 4420 Ashgrove Boulevard, including the annex building leased separately under the Pinecrest Holdings arrangement. Marrow & Doyle has serviced this account since 2018, initially under a smaller pilot contract limited to the east wing, before expanding to cover the full campus footprint in 2020. Over the past three renewal cycles, the vendor has maintained a service satisfaction rating averaging 4.2 out of 5 according to internal facilities surveys, with the most common feedback citing responsiveness to after-hours requests as a particular strength and invoice clarity as an area for continued improvement.

During the current review cycle, the vendor proposed a rate increase of 6.8 percent, citing rising costs of labor, fuel surcharges tied to waste transport, and increased material costs for cleaning supplies compliant with the company's updated sustainability standards. After internal benchmarking against two comparable vendors, Halvern Building Services and Costanza Facility Group, the Procurement team determined that Marrow & Doyle's proposed rate remained within the acceptable range, falling approximately 2 percent below the average of competing quotes for equivalent scope. Given the vendor's established performance history and the operational disruption typically associated with transitioning facilities vendors, the recommendation is to accept the proposed increase rather than pursue a competitive rebid at this time.

The renewal negotiation, led on the Colworth side by Vendor Relations Manager Theo Bramwell, resulted in several adjustments to the original contract language beyond the pricing update. Notably, the revised agreement introduces a quarterly service review meeting, to be attended by a designated representative from Marrow & Doyle and a member of the Facilities team, replacing the previous informal annual check-in. This change was proposed by Colworth in response to feedback gathered during last year's internal audit, which noted that issues such as delayed supply restocking or missed waste pickup windows were sometimes not surfaced to vendor management until several weeks after occurrence. The quarterly review structure is intended to shorten this feedback loop and provide a documented record of service issues and resolutions.

Additionally, the renewed contract updates the service level agreement language regarding response times for emergency requests, such as water leaks or heating system failures reported outside normal business hours. Under the previous agreement, Marrow & Doyle committed to a four-hour response window; the updated terms tighten this to three hours for the main campus building, while retaining the four-hour standard for the annex, reflecting the lower frequency of emergency requests historically logged at that location. Compliance with these revised windows will be tracked through the existing ticketing system maintained by the Facilities Help Desk, with monthly compliance summaries to be shared with the vendor as part of the new quarterly review process.

The contract also incorporates updated insurance and liability provisions consistent with Colworth's current risk management policy, including an increase in the required general liability coverage minimum from two million to three million dollars, a change that Marrow & Doyle's account representative, Priscilla Wexley, confirmed the vendor is prepared to meet without additional surcharge. Legal review of these updated provisions was completed by outside counsel at Danforth & Reeve LLP, with no outstanding concerns noted in their memorandum dated August 14.

Payment terms remain largely unchanged from the prior agreement, with invoices to be submitted monthly and payment due within thirty days of receipt. However, the renewed contract introduces a modest early payment discount of one percent for invoices settled within ten days, a provision requested by Marrow & Doyle to improve their cash flow predictability. Finance has indicated that utilizing this discount where feasible would be consistent with current departmental cash management practices, though it will not be treated as a mandatory target.

From a budgetary standpoint, the projected annual cost under the renewed agreement is estimated at approximately 412,000 dollars, up from the current 386,000 dollars, an increase that has been incorporated into the preliminary facilities budget for the coming fiscal year pending final committee approval. This figure assumes no significant change in campus square footage or service scope during the renewal period, though the agreement does include a standard clause allowing for prorated adjustments should the annex lease be terminated or additional space be added to the Colworth footprint.

Assuming no objections are raised during the Finance Committee's scheduled review on September 18, the renewed agreement is expected to be finalized and signed before the current contract's expiration date, ensuring continuity of service without a lapse. Theo Bramwell will coordinate the signing logistics with Marrow & Doyle's contracts department and will circulate the finalized document to relevant internal stakeholders, including Facilities, Finance, and Legal, for recordkeeping purposes. A follow-up summary confirming execution of the renewed contract will be distributed to the broader Operations team once signatures have been obtained from both parties.

VENDOR CONTRACT RENEWAL SUMMARY

Prepared by: Procurement Services Division, Halversen Industrial Group
Vendor: Braddock Supply & Logistics, LLC
Contract Reference Number: HIG-VC-2024-0187
Renewal Period: January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2027
Date of Preparation: October 22, 2024
Prepared for: Internal Vendor Management Committee Review

This document summarizes the terms, conditions, and internal recommendations associated with the renewal of the existing supply and distribution agreement between Halversen Industrial Group ("Halversen" or "the Company") and Braddock Supply & Logistics, LLC ("Braddock" or "the Vendor"). The purpose of this summary is to provide the Vendor Management Committee with a consolidated overview of the negotiated terms prior to final sign-off by the Chief Procurement Officer, Ms. Denise Okafor, and the Director of Operations, Mr. Colin Whitmore.

Background and Contract History

Braddock Supply & Logistics has served as a secondary-tier vendor for industrial packaging materials and warehouse distribution services since the original agreement was executed on March 4, 2019. The relationship has been renewed twice previously, most recently in 2022, with no material disputes or service interruptions recorded during either renewal period. Braddock currently supplies corrugated packaging, palletizing materials, and shrink-wrap products to four of Halversen's six regional distribution centers, located in Council Bluffs, Iowa; Terre Haute, Indiana; Macon, Georgia; and Spokane, Washington. Under the terms of the prior agreement, Braddock maintained an average on-time delivery rate of 96.3 percent across the contract period, with only minor deviations attributable to weather-related shipping delays in the winter of 2023.

The current renewal negotiations were initiated in July 2024 following a routine vendor performance review conducted by the Regional Operations Subcommittee. That review concluded that Braddock's pricing remained competitive relative to comparable vendors surveyed during the annual market benchmarking exercise, and that service quality metrics continued to meet or exceed internal thresholds established under Halversen's Vendor Performance Standards Policy, revised August 2021.

Summary of Negotiated Terms

The renewed agreement extends the relationship for a three-year term beginning January 1, 2025. Pricing under the new agreement reflects a 3.8 percent increase over current rates, which Braddock attributes primarily to rising raw material costs for recycled corrugate and increased freight surcharges tied to regional fuel indices. Procurement Services reviewed this proposed increase against the Company's internal cost-escalation guidelines and determined it to be within acceptable range, given that comparable vendors quoted increases ranging from 3.5 to 5.2 percent during the same benchmarking cycle.

The renewed contract preserves the existing service level agreement (SLA) structure, requiring a minimum on-time delivery rate of 95 percent measured on a quarterly basis, with financial penalties applicable if performance falls below 92 percent for two consecutive quarters. Braddock has agreed to an expanded reporting requirement under Section 6.2 of the renewed agreement, which will now require monthly delivery performance summaries to be submitted electronically to Halversen's Vendor Relations mailbox, rather than the quarterly reporting format used previously. This change was requested by Halversen's Operations team to allow for more granular tracking of seasonal delivery fluctuations.

Additionally, the renewed agreement includes an updated force majeure clause, expanding the definition to explicitly include disruptions caused by regional transportation infrastructure failures, consistent with revisions made across other Halversen vendor contracts following the 2023 review of supply chain resilience policies. No changes were made to the indemnification or insurance provisions, which remain consistent with the standard vendor contract template maintained by Legal Affairs.

Payment terms remain net-45 from invoice date, unchanged from the prior agreement. Braddock had initially requested a shift to net-30 terms citing internal cash flow considerations; however, this request was declined during negotiations in favor of maintaining consistency with Halversen's standard vendor payment cycle, which applies uniformly across all logistics and packaging suppliers under the Company's Accounts Payable Policy (Revision 4.1, January 2023).

Performance Considerations

The Vendor Management Committee's prior review identified no significant compliance concerns associated with Braddock. The vendor's certificate of insurance remains current through November 2025, and its Dun & Bradstreet financial health rating has remained stable at "Low Risk" for the past three reporting cycles. No safety incidents or regulatory citations involving Braddock's transportation subcontractors were reported during the current contract term. The Regional Operations Subcommittee noted, however, that Braddock's average response time to service inquiries submitted through the vendor support portal increased slightly during the second quarter of 2024, from an average of 4.2 hours to 6.7 hours. Braddock attributed this to a temporary staffing shortage in its customer service department, which has since been resolved according to information provided by the vendor's account representative, Mr. Aaron Delacroix.

Recommendation

Based on the consistent performance history, competitive pricing relative to market benchmarks, and absence of material compliance concerns, Procurement Services recommends approval of the renewal agreement as negotiated. The Vendor Management Committee is asked to review the attached redlined contract document (Appendix A) and provide any final comments no later than November 8, 2024, to allow sufficient time for execution prior to the December 1, 2024 internal deadline for renewals affecting Q1 2025 distribution schedules.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Fenwick Logistics Group ("the Company") recognizes that the nature of contemporary work has evolved considerably since the founding of our organization, and that many roles across our departments can be performed effectively outside of a traditional office environment. This section outlines the Company's expectations, procedures, and eligibility requirements for employees who wish to participate in remote work arrangements, whether on a full-time, hybrid, or occasional basis. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day probationary period, unless otherwise specified in an individual employment agreement or departmental exception approved by Human Resources.

Eligibility for remote work is determined primarily by job function and departmental need rather than tenure alone. Employees in roles that require regular in-person interaction with warehouse operations, such as those assigned to the Dornbridge Distribution Center or the Halvern Regional Fulfillment Hub, are generally not eligible for remote arrangements, given the physical nature of their responsibilities. Conversely, employees in administrative, analytical, customer support, and project coordination roles, including staff working on the Company's ongoing Meridian Connect supply chain visibility initiative, may be considered for hybrid or fully remote schedules upon manager approval. Requests for remote work must be submitted in writing to the employee's direct supervisor using the Remote Work Request Form available on the internal portal, and supervisors are expected to respond within ten business days.

Employees approved for hybrid schedules are generally expected to be present in the office a minimum of two days per week, though specific day requirements may vary by department and should be clarified directly with one's supervisor. The Logistics Analytics team under the direction of Departmental Manager Rosalind Ferrante, for instance, has historically required in-office presence on Tuesdays and Thursdays to accommodate weekly planning meetings related to the Company's freight optimization projects, while the Client Relations team led by Manager Desmond Okafor has adopted a more flexible rotating schedule based on client meeting demands. Employees should not assume that remote work arrangements approved for colleagues in other departments will automatically apply to their own situation, as departmental operational needs vary considerably.

All employees working remotely, whether on a full-time or hybrid basis, are expected to maintain the same standards of productivity, availability, and professionalism as they would in the office. This includes being reachable during standard core hours of 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, responding to internal communications in a timely manner, and attending virtual meetings with cameras enabled unless a specific accommodation has been granted. Employees are responsible for maintaining a workspace that is reasonably free from distraction and that allows for confidential handling of Company information, particularly for staff who regularly access client records through the Company's internal database systems. The Company reserves the right to request that an employee return to in-office work, temporarily or permanently, if performance concerns arise or if departmental needs change.

Employees working remotely are required to use Company-issued equipment whenever possible, including laptops, monitors, and headsets distributed through the IT Asset Management office under the supervision of Terrence Whitlock. Requests for additional equipment, such as ergonomic chairs or secondary monitors for home use, should be submitted through the Remote Work Equipment Request process and are subject to budgetary approval by the employee's department head. The Company does not reimburse employees for general household expenses such as internet service or electricity, though a modest monthly stipend of thirty-five dollars is provided to offset connectivity costs for employees approved for fully remote schedules exceeding three days per week. This stipend is processed automatically through payroll and does not require separate documentation unless the employee's remote status changes mid-cycle.

Employees who relocate while working remotely must notify Human Resources at least thirty days prior to the move, as relocation may affect tax withholding, eligibility for certain state-specific benefits, and in some cases the employee's continued eligibility for remote work depending on jurisdictional considerations. The Company has, in the past, been unable to accommodate relocations to states in which it does not currently hold appropriate business registration, and employees considering a move are strongly encouraged to consult with Human Resources Generalist Priya Nandakumar before finalizing any relocation plans.

Performance evaluations for remote and hybrid employees will follow the same general framework used for in-office staff, with particular attention paid to measurable outcomes, project milestones, and communication responsiveness rather than physical presence. Supervisors are encouraged to schedule regular one-on-one check-ins, whether in person or via video conference, to maintain consistent oversight and support for remote team members. Employees who feel that their remote arrangement is negatively affecting their visibility for promotional opportunities are encouraged to raise these concerns directly with their supervisor or with Human Resources, as the Company is committed to ensuring that remote work status does not disadvantage employees in matters of career advancement.

This policy is subject to periodic review and modification at the discretion of the Human Resources department in consultation with senior leadership. Any changes will be communicated to all employees through the internal announcements channel and will take effect no sooner than thirty days following notification, except where changes are required to comply with applicable law. Questions regarding this policy, including requests for exceptions based on individual circumstances, should be directed to the Human Resources office located on the third floor of the Company's Ashcombe Street headquarters or submitted electronically through the internal support ticketing system.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Holt Consulting Group recognizes that a balanced approach to work location and scheduling can contribute to employee productivity, satisfaction, and retention. This section outlines the guidelines governing remote work arrangements, flexible scheduling requests, and the expectations placed upon employees who participate in these arrangements. All employees, regardless of department or tenure, are expected to read and understand this policy in its entirety, and to consult with their direct supervisor or the Human Resources department at the Dunmore Office Park headquarters should any questions arise.

Eligibility for remote work arrangements is determined on a case-by-case basis and is contingent upon several factors, including but not limited to the nature of the employee's role, historical performance evaluations, and the operational needs of the team to which the employee belongs. Employees who wish to be considered for a remote or hybrid work arrangement must submit a Remote Work Request Form, available through the internal Meridian Holt intranet portal, to their manager no fewer than fourteen business days prior to the desired start date. Requests submitted with less notice may still be considered at the discretion of the manager and the relevant department head, but timely submission is strongly encouraged to allow for adequate planning and resource allocation.

Once a remote work arrangement has been approved, the employee and their manager will jointly establish a written agreement specifying the employee's expected working hours, the days on which remote work will occur, and any equipment or technology requirements necessary to perform the role effectively from a remote location. This agreement will be reviewed on a quarterly basis, coinciding with the standard performance check-in cycle, and may be revised or revoked if operational circumstances change or if the employee's performance does not meet the standards expected of their position. Employees on the Larkspur Analytics team, for example, have historically operated under a hybrid arrangement requiring in-office presence on Tuesdays and Thursdays, while employees supporting the Halden Municipal Services account have generally been required to maintain a fully in-office presence due to the nature of client interactions and data handling requirements associated with that account.

Employees participating in remote work arrangements are expected to maintain the same level of professionalism, responsiveness, and productivity as they would in an office setting. This includes being available during core business hours, which are defined as 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, unless an alternate schedule has been explicitly approved in writing by the employee's manager. Employees must ensure that they have a reliable internet connection and a suitable workspace free from excessive noise or distraction when participating in video conferences, client calls, or other work-related communications. Meridian Holt will provide a standard equipment stipend of up to four hundred dollars annually to remote and hybrid employees to assist with the purchase of ergonomic furniture, monitors, or other approved home office equipment, subject to submission of receipts through the Finance Department's reimbursement portal.

Communication expectations remain a cornerstone of this policy. Employees working remotely are required to respond to internal messages sent through the company's approved messaging platform, Connectway, within a reasonable timeframe during core business hours, generally understood to be within two hours absent extenuating circumstances such as scheduled meetings or approved time off. Managers are encouraged to establish clear norms with their direct reports regarding preferred communication channels and expected response times, and these norms should be documented within the team's shared operating procedures document, which is maintained on the internal knowledge base under the supervision of each department's designated administrator.

Flexible scheduling, as distinct from remote work, refers to arrangements in which an employee's daily start and end times deviate from the standard 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. schedule while the employee continues to work from a Meridian Holt office location. Employees seeking a flexible schedule must similarly submit a request through the intranet portal, and such requests are subject to the same fourteen-business-day notice period. Common examples of approved flexible scheduling arrangements include compressed workweeks, in which an employee works four ten-hour days rather than five eight-hour days, and staggered start times to accommodate childcare or eldercare responsibilities. The Client Services division, led by Regional Director Priyanka Deshmukh, has implemented a rotating flexible schedule pilot for its junior associates as part of the broader Project Comet initiative, and feedback from this pilot will be reviewed by the Human Resources Committee at the conclusion of the fiscal year to determine whether the arrangement should be expanded company-wide.

Employees should be aware that remote work and flexible scheduling arrangements are considered a privilege rather than an entitlement, and that Meridian Holt reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate any such arrangement at its sole discretion, with reasonable notice provided to the affected employee wherever possible. Abuse of remote work privileges, including but not limited to consistent unavailability during core hours, failure to meet project deadlines, or misrepresentation of hours worked, may result in the immediate revocation of remote work status and may be subject to further disciplinary action in accordance with the Employee Conduct Standards outlined in Section 4 of this handbook.

Questions regarding this policy, including requests for exceptions or accommodations related to documented medical conditions, should be directed to the Human Resources department via the internal ticketing system or by contacting HR Generalist Marcus Feldt directly at extension 2214. Meridian Holt Consulting Group is committed to periodically reviewing this policy to ensure it continues to reflect best practices in workplace flexibility while supporting the operational needs of our clients and the professional development of our employees.

SECTION 7: REMOTE WORK AND FLEXIBLE SCHEDULING POLICY

Meridian Falls Consulting Group ("the Company") recognizes that a balanced approach to work arrangements contributes to employee satisfaction and operational continuity. This policy establishes the framework under which employees may request remote work privileges or flexible scheduling arrangements, and it outlines the responsibilities of both the employee and the Company in maintaining productivity standards under such arrangements. This policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day probationary period, as determined by their respective department managers.

Eligibility for remote work arrangements is determined on a case-by-case basis and is subject to approval by the employee's direct supervisor and, where applicable, the Human Resources department. Factors considered in evaluating a remote work request include, but are not limited to, the nature of the employee's job duties, the employee's demonstrated ability to work independently, prior performance evaluations, and the operational needs of the department. Employees in client-facing roles, such as those within the Client Relations division under the supervision of Ms. Doreen Achterberg, may be subject to additional restrictions given the nature of their responsibilities, including the requirement to be present on-site during scheduled client visits or quarterly review meetings.

Employees seeking to establish a remote work arrangement must submit a Remote Work Request Form, available through the internal employee portal, no less than fourteen business days prior to the desired start date. The form requires the employee to specify the proposed schedule, the primary location from which remote work will be performed, and a brief justification for the request. Requests will be reviewed by the employee's supervisor within five business days of submission, and a written response, whether approval or denial, will be provided through the internal messaging system. Employees whose requests are denied may resubmit a revised request after a period of thirty calendar days, unless circumstances materially change sooner.

Employees who are approved for remote work are expected to maintain the same standards of productivity, availability, and professionalism as they would in an on-site setting. This includes being reachable during core business hours, defined as 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. in the employee's designated time zone, unless alternative hours have been explicitly approved in writing by the employee's supervisor. Employees are further expected to attend all scheduled virtual meetings with cameras enabled unless a specific exception has been granted, and to respond to internal communications within a reasonable timeframe, generally understood to be no more than four business hours during the standard workweek.

The Company will provide reasonable accommodations to support remote work arrangements, including a one-time stipend for home office equipment as outlined in Section 12 of this handbook, titled "Equipment and Reimbursement Policies." Employees are responsible for maintaining a workspace that is free from significant distractions and that allows for confidential handling of Company materials, particularly for employees who regularly access client financial records or proprietary business strategies. Any breach of confidentiality resulting from inadequate workspace security may result in disciplinary action as outlined in Section 15, "Confidentiality and Data Protection Standards."

Flexible scheduling, distinct from remote work, refers to arrangements in which an employee's start and end times may vary from the standard 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. schedule, provided that the employee still completes the required number of weekly hours and remains available during core business hours. Employees interested in flexible scheduling should discuss their proposed arrangement directly with their supervisor rather than submitting a formal request form, though supervisors reserve the right to require written confirmation of the agreed-upon schedule for record-keeping purposes. Mr. Foster Kallenbrenner, Director of Operations, has noted in prior department memos that flexible scheduling arrangements should be reviewed periodically to ensure they continue to serve both the employee's needs and the Company's operational requirements.

Employees participating in either remote work or flexible scheduling arrangements remain subject to all other Company policies, including those governing attendance, performance evaluation, and code of conduct. Supervisors are expected to evaluate remote and flexible employees using the same criteria applied to on-site staff, and no employee shall be penalized or disadvantaged in performance reviews solely on the basis of their work arrangement, provided that performance expectations continue to be met. Any perceived inequity in this regard should be reported to Human Resources through the standard grievance procedure outlined in Section 22.

The Company reserves the right to modify or revoke remote work and flexible scheduling arrangements at its discretion, particularly in cases where business needs change, performance concerns arise, or the employee's role evolves to require greater on-site presence. Whenever possible, the Company will provide at least two weeks' notice prior to revoking an existing arrangement, except in circumstances involving urgent business needs or disciplinary matters, in which case shorter notice may be given. Employees who disagree with a decision to revoke their arrangement may request a meeting with their supervisor and a Human Resources representative to discuss the matter further, though such a meeting does not guarantee reinstatement of the prior arrangement.

This policy will be reviewed annually by the Human Resources department, in coordination with departmental leadership, to ensure it continues to reflect the operational realities of the Company and the evolving expectations of its workforce. Questions regarding this policy may be directed to the Human Resources office or to an employee's immediate supervisor.

This document presents a summary of existing literature pertaining to internal communication practices within mid-sized enterprises, with particular emphasis on studies published between 2014 and 2023. The review was commissioned to inform ongoing revisions to the internal communications framework at Halveston Group and to provide a defensible evidentiary basis for recommendations forthcoming in subsequent planning documents. The scope of this review was limited to peer-reviewed studies, industry white papers, and select case analyses that address communication structures in organizations employing between two hundred and two thousand personnel, as this range most closely approximates the operational scale of comparable firms within our sector.

The foundational work in this area is generally attributed to Marguerite Ashcombe, whose 2015 longitudinal study of communication latency in regional manufacturing firms established much of the vocabulary still used in later research. Ashcombe's framework distinguishes between "vertical transmission delay," referring to the time elapsed between decision-making at senior levels and awareness at operational levels, and "lateral diffusion friction," which describes the comparatively slower spread of information across departments of similar hierarchical standing. Ashcombe's data, drawn from eleven firms in the Midlands region, suggested that vertical transmission delay averaged 4.2 days in organizations without dedicated internal communications staff, compared to 1.6 days in organizations with such personnel. While her sample size has been criticized as insufficiently broad to support generalization, the conceptual distinction she introduced has proven durable and is referenced in nearly all subsequent literature reviewed here.

Building on Ashcombe's typology, a research team led by Desmond Okonkwo-Reyes at the Fennimore Institute for Organizational Studies conducted a broader cross-sectional survey in 2018, encompassing sixty-three firms across four industry sectors. Okonkwo-Reyes and colleagues found that lateral diffusion friction was more strongly correlated with physical office layout than with formal reporting structures, a finding that has since informed a modest but persistent literature on open-plan versus segmented office design. Their study also introduced the concept of "communication redundancy tolerance," which measures the degree to which an organization can absorb repeated or overlapping messaging without generating employee fatigue or disengagement. This concept has been taken up with varying degrees of enthusiasm by later researchers, some of whom argue it is difficult to operationalize consistently across different organizational cultures.

A subsequent and frequently cited contribution comes from the work of Priya Vandermolen, whose 2019 monograph examined the role of middle management as an information relay layer. Vandermolen's central argument, supported by interview data from forty-two middle managers across twelve organizations, is that middle managers frequently function as informal editors of upward and downward communication, selectively emphasizing or omitting content based on their own assessment of relevance to their teams. This editorial function, she contends, is neither uniformly beneficial nor uniformly detrimental, but rather contingent on the manager's tenure, training, and perceived autonomy within the organization. Vandermolen's work has been influential in shifting subsequent research away from purely structural analyses of communication flow and toward a greater consideration of individual discretion within those structures.

The literature also contains a smaller but methodologically rigorous strand of research focused specifically on the adoption of digital communication tools. A 2020 study by Anders Lindqvist and Fatima Benzarti examined the introduction of unified messaging platforms in fourteen mid-sized firms and found that adoption alone did not reliably reduce vertical transmission delay unless accompanied by explicit changes to meeting cadence and documentation practices. Their findings suggest that technological interventions, while frequently proposed as straightforward solutions to communication inefficiency, tend to produce measurable improvement only when integrated with corresponding procedural adjustments. This conclusion is broadly consistent with earlier work by Okonkwo-Reyes, who similarly cautioned against treating tool adoption as a substitute for structural or cultural change.

More recent contributions have begun to examine the intersection of internal communication practices with employee retention outcomes. A 2022 study conducted by the consultancy firm Bramwell & Cortez, though not peer-reviewed in the traditional academic sense, has nonetheless been cited with some frequency in subsequent grey literature. Their analysis of exit interview data from over three hundred departing employees across nine client organizations suggested a moderate correlation between self-reported communication clarity and stated intention to remain with an employer, though the authors themselves note that correlation of this kind is difficult to disentangle from broader satisfaction measures. This caveat is echoed in a smaller 2023 study by Naomi Kirchner-Osei, who attempted a more controlled replication using a matched sample of forty employees and found the correlation to be weaker than Bramwell & Cortez had reported, though still present.

Taken together, the literature reviewed here points toward several recurring themes that are likely relevant to internal planning at Halveston Group. First, structural interventions such as the appointment of dedicated communications staff appear to produce measurable reductions in transmission delay, though the magnitude of this effect varies considerably by study. Second, the role of middle management as an informal editorial layer warrants explicit consideration in any redesign of communication protocols, as this layer's discretion can either support or undermine formal messaging strategies depending on how it is managed. Third, technological solutions, while useful, should not be treated as sufficient on their own, and are best implemented alongside corresponding changes to procedural cadence. Finally, while a link between communication clarity and retention appears plausible based on available evidence, the strength of this relationship remains uncertain and would benefit from further internal study before being incorporated into any formal business case. Tenants in Building A should expect brief service notices posted in elevator lobbies no fewer than 48 hours prior to any planned shutdown, consistent with the notification policy established after the disruption experienced during last year's unplanned outage on the fourth floor.

Elevator maintenance will remain under contract with Thornbury Vertical Transport, whose technicians conduct monthly safety inspections on the second Tuesday of each month across all buildings except Building D, where the newer Schaeffler-model elevators installed during the 2022 renovation are inspected on a bimonthly basis per manufacturer recommendation. Landscaping and exterior grounds upkeep, contracted through Prairie Edge Grounds Management, will follow the standard growing-season schedule, with mowing and trimming occurring weekly from April through October and biweekly during the remaining months when conditions permit. The irrigation system serving the courtyard between Buildings B and C underwent repair last spring following the line rupture near the east fountain, and Prairie Edge has confirmed that the repaired section will be monitored monthly through the end of the calendar year as a precautionary measure. Snow and ice removal services, provided under a separate seasonal rider with the same vendor, will be activated automatically once accumulation forecasts exceed one inch, with priority clearing given to the main entrances of Buildings A and B due to higher pedestrian traffic volumes documented in last year's foot-traffic study conducted by the property management office.

Janitorial services for all common areas, restrooms, and lobby spaces will continue under the agreement with Halberd Cleaning Solutions, with nightly service Monday through Friday and a reduced weekend schedule limited to restroom restocking and lobby floor care. Building D's shared conference facilities on the third floor, given their frequent use for tenant events and the recent addition of the Meridian Room booked through the property's new reservation portal, will receive supplemental daytime cleaning on days when bookings are confirmed, coordinated directly between Halberd's site supervisor and the reservation desk to avoid overlap with ongoing meetings. Any special cleaning requests outside the standard scope, such as post-event deep cleaning or carpet extraction, should be submitted through the facilities request form at least five business days in advance to allow for proper vendor scheduling.

Fire suppression and life safety system inspections, mandated under state code and overseen by Redcliff Fire Protection, will occur semiannually in April and October, with sprinkler head inspections, alarm panel testing, and emergency lighting checks conducted in sequence across all four buildings over a two-week window. Building superintendents will coordinate with individual tenants to schedule brief access windows for suite-level inspections where required, and any suite found to have obstructed sprinkler heads or blocked panel access during inspection will receive a written notice requesting remediation within ten business days, consistent with the property's standing safety compliance policy adopted after the annual audit two years ago.

Section 7: Remote Work and Flexible Scheduling Policy

Meridian Fenwick Group ("the Company") recognizes that the modern workplace has evolved to accommodate a variety of working arrangements that support both operational needs and employee well-being. This section outlines the guidelines, expectations, and procedures governing remote work and flexible scheduling for all eligible employees across the Company's divisions, including Operations, Client Services, and the Product Development team currently supporting the Halstead Initiative.

Eligibility for remote work arrangements is determined by an employee's role, tenure, and performance history, as well as the operational requirements of the employee's department. Generally, employees who have completed a minimum of ninety calendar days of continuous employment and who maintain a satisfactory performance rating on their most recent review are eligible to submit a request for a remote or hybrid work arrangement. Requests must be submitted in writing to the employee's direct supervisor using the Remote Work Request Form, available through the internal HR portal maintained by the People Operations team. Supervisors are expected to respond to such requests within ten business days, taking into consideration team coverage needs, client-facing obligations, and the nature of the employee's day-to-day responsibilities.

Employees whose roles are approved for hybrid arrangements are generally expected to be present in the office a minimum of two days per week, with specific in-office days to be coordinated at the department level to ensure adequate team overlap and collaboration. For example, members of the Client Solutions team led by Regional Director Priya Anand are currently required to maintain in-office presence on Tuesdays and Thursdays to accommodate weekly client strategy sessions, while the Marketing Analytics group under Senior Manager Douglas Ferro has adopted a more flexible model in which in-office days rotate on a monthly basis depending on project deadlines, including ongoing work related to the Brightline campaign rollout.

Employees approved for fully remote arrangements are expected to maintain a stable and professional home working environment that supports uninterrupted participation in meetings, timely response to communications, and secure handling of Company data. This includes maintaining a reliable internet connection with a minimum upload and download speed as specified in the Company's IT Standards Bulletin, as well as ensuring that any Company-issued equipment, including laptops, monitors, and peripheral devices, is used in accordance with the Acceptable Use Policy outlined in Section 12 of this handbook. Employees working remotely are also responsible for safeguarding confidential Company information and client data by following the data security protocols distributed by the Information Security team, including the use of approved virtual private network connections when accessing internal systems.

Core working hours for all employees, regardless of work location, are established as 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. local time, during which employees are expected to be available for meetings, calls, and collaborative work unless otherwise arranged with their supervisor. Outside of core hours, employees may exercise flexibility in structuring their workday to accommodate personal obligations, provided that they meet all deadlines, attend scheduled meetings, and complete their standard forty-hour workweek, or the equivalent for part-time employees as defined in their individual employment agreements. Employees who anticipate a need to deviate from their normal schedule on a given day, whether due to a medical appointment, family obligation, or other personal matter, are asked to notify their supervisor in advance where possible and to log the adjusted hours in the timekeeping system administered by the Payroll department.

Overall, the third quarter reflected a period of moderate, steady performance across most business units, with results generally consistent with the projections established during the mid-year planning review conducted in June. Total consolidated revenue for the quarter reached $48.3 million, representing a 2.1 percent increase over the second quarter and a 4.6 percent increase over the same quarter in the prior fiscal year. This growth was driven primarily by continued expansion within the Logistics and Distribution division, which posted revenue of $19.7 million, up from $18.4 million in the previous quarter. Division Director Corinne Ashby attributed this increase to the successful onboarding of two mid-sized regional clients in the Midwest corridor, as well as improved route efficiency following the rollout of the updated scheduling software implemented in May.

The Manufacturing and Assembly division reported revenue of $14.2 million, a modest decline of 1.3 percent from the second quarter. This decrease was largely attributed to scheduled maintenance downtime at the Fairhaven production facility, which resulted in an estimated 240 hours of reduced line capacity during the month of August. Facility Manager Owen Delacroix noted that the maintenance work, which included replacement of aging conveyor infrastructure, was completed on schedule and is expected to improve throughput capacity by approximately 6 percent beginning in the fourth quarter. No safety incidents were reported during the maintenance period, and the division maintained its full compliance record with applicable occupational safety standards.

The Professional Services division, under the leadership of Senior Vice President Miriam Okafor, posted revenue of $9.8 million, representing growth of 5.4 percent over the prior quarter. This growth was primarily driven by an increase in consulting engagements within the healthcare administration sector, where the division secured three new multi-year contracts during the quarter. Staffing levels within the division increased modestly, with twelve new associate-level hires onboarded across the Denver and Charlotte offices to support the expanded client base. Client retention rates within the division remained strong at 94 percent, consistent with historical averages for this business line.

The Retail Solutions division experienced the most significant softness in the quarter, with revenue declining 3.7 percent to $4.6 million. Regional Manager Theodore Vance indicated that this decline was largely attributable to broader softening in consumer discretionary spending observed across several of the division's key markets, particularly in the Southeastern region. The division has initiated a review of its promotional pricing strategy in response to these trends, with recommendations expected to be presented to the Executive Committee during the fourth quarter planning cycle. Inventory turnover ratios within the division remained within acceptable ranges, though slightly below the twelve-month trailing average.

Operating expenses across the organization totaled $41.9 million for the quarter, representing an operating margin of approximately 13.3 percent, consistent with the company's target range of 12 to 15 percent established in the annual operating plan. Administrative and overhead costs remained flat relative to the prior quarter, reflecting continued adherence to the cost containment measures introduced at the start of the fiscal year. Notable expense items during the quarter included the completion of the Fairhaven facility maintenance project, previously discussed, as well as continued investment in the enterprise resource planning system upgrade, which remains on track for full implementation by the second quarter of fiscal year 2025. Project Lead Simone Kavanagh reported that the upgrade is currently within budget and approximately 68 percent complete.

Headcount across the organization stood at 1,842 employees as of the end of the quarter, reflecting a net increase of 24 positions compared to the previous quarter. This growth was concentrated primarily within the Professional Services and Logistics divisions, consistent with the revenue trends described above. The Human Resources Department, led by Director Felix Bramwell, reported voluntary turnover of 3.1 percent for the quarter, a slight improvement from the 3.4 percent reported in the second quarter. Employee engagement survey results, administered in early September, indicated overall satisfaction scores consistent with prior periods, with the most notable area of improvement cited as internal communication practices following the rollout of the updated intranet platform in July.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, management anticipates continued stability in overall performance, with particular attention to monitoring consumer spending trends within the Retail Solutions division and completing the remaining phases of the enterprise resource planning upgrade. The Executive Committee has directed each division to submit updated fourth-quarter forecasts by October 15, incorporating any adjustments related to seasonal demand patterns and ongoing capital projects. A comprehensive year-end performance summary, including preliminary guidance for fiscal year 2025, will be prepared for presentation to the Board of Directors during the December meeting.

# Facilities Maintenance Schedule — Riverbend Corporate Campus
## Prepared by the Office of Facilities Management, Q3–Q4 Cycle

This document outlines the recurring and scheduled maintenance activities for the Riverbend Corporate Campus buildings, encompassing the Alder Wing, the Birchwood Annex, and the Central Plaza structure. It is intended to serve as a reference for department heads, vendor coordinators, and building tenants regarding anticipated service windows, responsible personnel, and expected disruptions to normal operations. All timelines are approximate and subject to adjustment based on vendor availability and weather conditions, particularly for exterior work.

Routine HVAC inspections will continue on their established quarterly rhythm, with the next cycle beginning the second week of the reporting period. Marlene Attaway, Senior Mechanical Systems Technician, will oversee inspection of rooftop units on the Alder Wing, while contracted services from Kestrel Mechanical Group will handle the air handling units located in the Birchwood Annex basement level. Building occupants should expect brief, intermittent reductions in airflow on affected floors during inspection windows, typically lasting no more than ninety minutes per zone. Notification signage will be posted at elevator banks no less than forty-eight hours in advance, in accordance with standard tenant communication protocol.

Elevator maintenance for the Central Plaza structure has been scheduled with Halloway Vertical Transport Services for the third week of the cycle. Two of the four passenger elevators will be taken offline sequentially to allow for cable inspection, lubrication, and door sensor recalibration. Facilities coordinator Dennis Okafor will serve as the primary point of contact for scheduling conflicts arising from reduced elevator capacity, and he has requested that any department anticipating large deliveries or equipment moves during this window contact his office at least five business days prior so that alternate routing through the freight elevator can be arranged.

Landscaping and grounds maintenance will proceed under the existing contract with Fennimore Grounds Care, with mowing and edging occurring on a biweekly basis through the end of the growing season. Irrigation system testing is scheduled for the first Tuesday of each month, conducted jointly by Fennimore staff and campus facilities personnel to confirm zone-by-zone functionality ahead of seasonal shutdown planning in late autumn. Any visible leaks, broken sprinkler heads, or drainage concerns identified during these tests will be logged in the facilities maintenance tracking system and addressed within the following two weeks, barring parts availability issues.

The fire suppression and alarm systems across all three buildings are due for their annual certification inspection, to be performed by Corrigan Life Safety Consultants during the fourth week of the cycle. This inspection will require brief testing of alarm horns and strobes on each floor, and tenants are advised that these tests may produce audible alerts lasting several seconds at a time between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. on the days scheduled. A full building evacuation is not anticipated as part of this inspection; however, fire wardens on each floor will be notified in advance so they may inform their respective teams and address any questions about the process.

Plumbing system checks, including inspection of restroom fixtures, kitchen area drains, and the boiler room in the Alder Wing sub-basement, will be handled internally by the facilities maintenance team under the supervision of Teresa Vance, Facilities Operations Lead. This work is generally low-impact and unlikely to require closure of restroom facilities, though isolated instances may necessitate temporary signage directing occupants to alternate restrooms on adjacent floors. Any anticipated water shutoffs exceeding fifteen minutes will be communicated via the internal facilities notification email distribution list at least twenty-four hours beforehand.

Painting and minor cosmetic repair work in common areas, including the main lobby of the Birchwood Annex and the second-floor conference corridor of the Alder Wing, has been tentatively scheduled for a weekend in the latter half of the cycle to minimize disruption to regular business operations. This work will be performed by Castellane Painting & Restoration and is expected to span two consecutive days. Furniture in affected areas will be temporarily relocated by the facilities team the preceding Friday afternoon, and occupants of nearby offices are asked to remove any personal items from shared shelving in these corridors prior to that time.

Parking structure lighting retrofits, transitioning remaining fixtures to LED units, will be carried out in phases by Brightline Electrical Contractors over a three-week span. Work will occur primarily during evening and overnight hours to reduce interference with daytime parking access, though a limited number of spaces on the affected levels will be cordoned off during active work periods. Campus security has been briefed on the schedule and will adjust patrol patterns accordingly to maintain adequate lighting coverage in unaffected areas during the transition.

Window washing for all exterior glass surfaces on the Central Plaza structure is scheduled for a single day toward the end of the cycle, weather permitting, and will be conducted by Summit Facade Services using rope access techniques. Departments located on the exterior-facing offices of floors four through nine should expect intermittent visual obstruction from equipment and personnel during this window, and blinds may be lowered at the discretion of individual occupants if preferred. Rescheduling due to inclement weather will be communicated as early as possible, typically the morning of the originally planned date.

Finally, this schedule will be reviewed and updated at the close of the current cycle to incorporate any carried-over items, vendor rescheduling, or newly identified maintenance needs surfaced through the facilities work order system. Department heads with recurring concerns not addressed in this document are encouraged to submit them through the standard work order portal rather than through direct email, as this ensures proper tracking and prioritization. This memorandum summarizes the terms and considerations associated with the renewal of the vendor services agreement between Halstead Bridge Manufacturing Co. ("the Company") and Corvale Logistics Solutions, Inc. ("Corvale" or "the Vendor"), covering the provision of third-party warehousing, inventory management, and regional freight coordination services. The current agreement, originally executed on March 14, 2021, and subsequently amended on two occasions, is set to expire on November 30 of this year unless a renewal instrument is executed prior to that date. This summary is intended for internal review by the Procurement Committee and the Office of Vendor Relations, and it reflects input gathered from the Operations, Finance, and Legal departments during the preceding quarter.

Under the existing arrangement, Corvale has provided warehousing services out of its Midvale Regional Distribution Center, along with periodic freight consolidation support for shipments originating from the Company's Danforth Assembly Plant. Performance under the current term has been generally satisfactory, with quarterly service-level reports indicating an average on-time delivery rate of 96.3 percent and a damaged-goods incident rate below the contractual threshold of 0.5 percent. Minor deviations were noted in the second and third quarters of this year, attributable primarily to a temporary staffing shortage at the Midvale facility following seasonal turnover, though Corvale's account management team, led by Regional Director Priya Anand, addressed the matter through supplemental staffing arrangements and did not require formal escalation under the dispute resolution clause of the agreement.

Following a review of comparable vendor rates in the regional market, conducted by the Company's Sourcing Analyst, Marcus Feldt, it was determined that Corvale's proposed renewal pricing remains within an acceptable range relative to competitor benchmarks, specifically Aldermere Freight Partners and Boyle & Sons Logistics, both of which were considered as alternative providers during the preliminary renewal discussions. Corvale's proposed rate structure for the renewal term reflects a 3.8 percent increase over current pricing, attributed by the Vendor to rising fuel surcharges and increased labor costs at the Midvale facility. This increase is broadly consistent with inflationary adjustments observed across the logistics sector during the past twelve months and falls slightly below the average increase requested by competing vendors during the sourcing review.

The proposed renewal term spans thirty-six months, commencing December 1 and concluding November 30 three years hence, with an option for a further twenty-four-month extension subject to mutual written agreement no later than ninety days prior to expiration. The renewal draft, prepared by the Company's outside counsel at Whitfield & Corrigan LLP, retains the substantive structure of the prior agreement, including the existing indemnification provisions, insurance requirements, and confidentiality clauses, while introducing several updates recommended by the Legal department. Notably, the renewal incorporates a revised force majeure clause reflecting recent guidance on supply chain disruptions, an updated data security addendum consistent with the Company's revised vendor cybersecurity policy adopted earlier this year, and a modified termination-for-convenience provision reducing the required notice period from ninety to sixty days, a change requested by the Company's Finance department to preserve greater flexibility in future budget planning cycles.

Corvale has additionally proposed the inclusion of a new performance incentive structure, under which the Vendor would receive a modest rebate on quarterly service fees if on-time delivery rates exceed 98 percent and damaged-goods incidents remain below 0.3 percent for two consecutive quarters. The Operations department has reviewed this proposal favorably, noting that it aligns incentives without introducing undue financial risk to the Company, and recommends its inclusion in the final renewal agreement, subject to minor adjustments to the measurement methodology to ensure consistency with the Company's existing internal reporting standards.

Finance has confirmed that the renewal, inclusive of the proposed rate increase, remains within the budgeted allocation for third-party logistics services for the upcoming fiscal year, as approved during the Q3 budget planning session. The Vendor Relations Office has further confirmed that Corvale maintains current and valid certifications required under the Company's vendor compliance program, including its liability insurance coverage, its OSHA compliance documentation, and its updated business continuity plan, copies of which have been placed in the vendor file maintained by the Compliance department.

Internal stakeholders were consulted throughout the review process, including representatives from Operations, Finance, Legal, and the Danforth Assembly Plant management team, all of whom expressed general support for renewal, citing the stability of the existing relationship, Corvale's responsiveness to prior service issues, and the absence of significant unresolved disputes over the life of the current agreement. No stakeholder raised concerns sufficient to warrant a formal request for competitive rebidding at this time, though it was noted that the Sourcing team will continue to monitor market rates on an annual basis to ensure the Company's continued access to competitive terms.

Based on the foregoing considerations, it is recommended that the Procurement Committee approve the renewal of the vendor services agreement with Corvale Logistics Solutions, Inc. on the terms outlined above, subject to final review and sign-off by the Legal department and confirmation of budgetary allocation by the Finance department. Upon approval, the Office of Vendor Relations will coordinate execution of the renewal instrument with Corvale's contracts administrator, Daniel Osei, and will circulate the fully executed agreement to all relevant departments prior to the expiration of the current term. A follow-up review of vendor performance under the renewed agreement is scheduled for the second quarter of next year, consistent with the Company's standard vendor oversight cadence.

# Terms of Service Update Summary

**Effective Date: March 17, 2025**

**Prepared by: Meridian Cloud Solutions, Inc. — Legal & Compliance Department**

This document summarizes recent updates to the Terms of Service ("Terms") governing use of Meridian Cloud Solutions' hosting, storage, and collaboration products (collectively, the "Services"). These updates take effect on the date noted above and apply to all existing and future customers, including those operating under legacy agreements executed prior to January 2023. Customers are encouraged to review the full Terms of Service document in its entirety, available through the account administration portal, as this summary is intended for informational purposes only and does not supersede the complete legal text.

The most significant revision in this update concerns Section 4.2, "Data Retention and Deletion Practices." Previously, the Terms specified that account data would be retained for a period of ninety (90) days following account termination or non-renewal before permanent deletion. Under the revised language, this retention window has been extended to one hundred eighty (180) days to accommodate customer requests for data recovery following inadvertent cancellations or billing lapses. Customers who wish to opt out of the extended retention period and request immediate deletion upon termination may do so by submitting a written request to the Data Governance team, care of Assistant Compliance Officer RenataHolloway, whose contact details are provided in Appendix C of the full agreement.

Section 6, governing "Service Level Commitments," has also been revised to clarify the calculation methodology for monthly uptime percentages. The prior language was found to be ambiguous regarding scheduled maintenance windows, and several customers, including representatives from Halvorsen Logistics and the Bramwell Group, raised questions during the customer advisory session held in November 2024. The updated language now explicitly excludes pre-announced maintenance periods of four hours or less from uptime calculations, provided that Meridian Cloud Solutions furnishes at least seventy-two hours' advance notice through the customer's designated administrative contact. Maintenance windows exceeding four hours, or those conducted without adequate notice, will continue to count against the monthly uptime guarantee as before.
